text: A heat pump moves heat rather than generating it. In winter, it extracts thermal energy from the cold outdoor air and transfers it indoors using a refrigerant cycle. Conversely, in summer, it reverses the process to pull heat from inside the home and release it outside. By circulating this refrigerant through a compressor and expansion valve, the system efficiently heats or cools spaces, often achieving higher energy efficiency than traditional electric resistance heaters.
